name: grin
desc: Minimal implementation of the Mimblewimble protocol
why: A minimal Mimblewimble implementation is a rare look at an unusual cryptocurrency protocol design.

brief.what_it_is: Grin is an in-progress implementation of the Mimblewimble protocol, a privacy-preserving digital currency built by developers around the world. The README describes it as a clean, minimal codebase that aims to stay that way. The homepage frames Grin as a currency with no amounts and no addresses, where transactions can be aggregated and relayed through a subset of peers before broadcast. The brew formula installs a single executable named grin. The README does not say what the command takes in or prints, so input and output formats are unknown from these pages.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents Grin as a privacy-preserving currency that is not controlled by any company, foundation or individual, with fair distribution and no ICO, pre-mine or founder's reward. The homepage says Mimblewimble lets past transaction data be removed without losing security, so the chain does not collapse under stored data.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the protocol hides amounts and gives scaling advantages, and that transaction fees depend on the number of outputs created or destroyed and total transaction size. Proof of work uses Cuckoo Cycle in two variants, Cuckaroo (ASIC-resistant) and Cuckatoo (ASIC-targeted), with a one-minute block time and a smooth difficulty adjustment curve. The homepage adds that a new transaction is relayed among a subset of peers before wide broadcast to hide its origin. The detailed mechanism is in doc/intro.md, which I did not fetch.
brief.install_notes: The README points to doc/build.md for building and running Grin, which I did not fetch, so no build or run commands were seen. Nothing in the README or homepage mentions accounts, hardware or a runtime beyond what the build docs would cover. Brew installs it with no extra caveats from the formula. The README does not mention first-run configuration.
brief.standout: The homepage and README describe a Mimblewimble coin, a protocol that drops transaction amounts and addresses and can prune historical data, which is unusual next to Bitcoin-style designs. The project also keeps its implementation deliberately small and says so in its philosophy section.
brief.status: The README says Grin is live on mainnet and that much remains to be done, and it invites contributions. It links a mailing list archive for the latest status. I saw no release date or last commit date on the pages I read, so recency is unknown. The GitHub page shows a release badge and CI badges, but I did not see their values.
brief.caveats: The README says many characteristics of the protocol are still undefined and that the project is in progress. The brew description and scout note say 'minimal implementation' and that matches the README's own wording. The homepage's claim of 'no amounts and no addresses' is the site's framing and was not checked against code. Licensing is Apache License v2.0. I did not verify the build pain or platform support because the build docs were not read.
quotes: Grin is an in-progress implementation of the Mimblewimble protocol.
Clean and minimal implementation, and aiming to stay as such.
Grin likes itself small and easy on the eyes.
